wacc.formula: WACC = wₑ × kₑ + w_d × k_d × (1 − t);  kₑ = r_f + β × ERP
steps: β (Blume-adjusted) = 0.67 × raw β 1.74 + 0.33 = 1.50  (104 weekly returns vs SPY, R² 0.24)

methods.formula: 10-year Monte Carlo: revenue growth switches between high / steady / decline regimes by a Markov chain; margin drifts by regime; value = Σ discounted FCFF − SBC + terminal, per share
assumptions: its own history + the panel prior (markov.json)
methods.fit: It has a DCF and enough quarters of revenue history to estimate how often its growth switches regime.

methods.formula: FCFF = EBIT × (1 − t) + D&A − capex − ΔWC;  EV = Σ FCFF/(1+WACC)^t + TV/(1+WACC)^5;  TV = NOPAT₆ × (1 − g ÷ ROIC) ÷ (WACC − g);  value = (EV − debt + cash − claims) ÷ shares
steps: growth by year 22%, 18%, 14%, 10%, 6%; EBIT margin 0.3%; D&A 3.3% of revenue; capex 2.4% of revenue; ΔWC 10% of each revenue increase
Monte Carlo: 2,000 scenarios, 10th–90th percentile −$39.53 – $23.18; P(value > price) = 26%

methods.formula: Stage-weighted value = Σ weight × central value of the stage's methods (weights renormalized over the methods available)
steps: 31% × −$5.05 (DCF — Monte Carlo 10th–90th percentile) + 31% × −$2.97 (Outside view — base-rate Monte Carlo) + 19% × $67.71 (EV/Sales vs Rule of 40 (all-company fit)) + 19% × $37.31 (EV/Sales vs peers) = $17.19
assumptions: fixed by stage before any result was seen (base_rates.STAGES)
methods.fit: Its stage is “High growth” — revenue growth +22.1% — which fixes these methods and their weights in advance.

methods.formula: EPV = adjusted earnings ÷ WACC − net debt;  adjusted earnings = normalized EBIT × (1 − t) + D&A − maintenance capex;  normalized EBIT = average margin × revenue
steps: normalized EBIT = 3.2% × $2.07B = $65.26M  (average EBIT margin of the last 4 years (9%, 4%, 1%, -1%))
maintenance capex = $0  (capex $49.51M − growth capex (PP&E $331.3M ÷ revenue × revenue gain $374.3M = $49.51M))
